Subject: Pilot capacity ask — APAC go-live + EU standby

Jonas / team,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We're aiming to kick off a 6–8 week APAC pilot in Singapore for OrionAI's customer-facing assistant. Primary traffic profile attached (OrionAI_Pilot_traffic_forecast.csv). Quick highlights: baseline ~120 qps, short burst windows up to ~600 qps (20 minute bursts).

Requests from our side: 
- Recommendation for an initial dedicated pool in APAC to meet 99th-pt latency <120ms for token generation.
- Minimal standby in EU for failover (warm nodes that can spin up).
- Cost ballpark (monthly commit + burst), and a simple scale-trigger proposal (what metrics should drive moving from pilot -> scale).

Procurement will need an SOW with the capacity plan attached to the PO. Can you share a first draft by EOD tomorrow?

Appreciate it,
Amit Shah
Head of Platform, OrionAI
amit@orionai.com
+1 415 555 0189

Date: Wed, 10 Mar 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot capacity ask — APAC go-live + EU standby

Amit — thanks, attached is an initial sizing workbook (jonas_regional_sizing_v1.xlsx). TL;DR: start pilot with an 8 GPU dedicated pool in SG (A100-80GB equiv), split across two 4-GPU nodes to reduce single-node cache hot spots. Add an 8-GPU burst slab for peak windows. EU standby: 6 GPUs reserved but largely warm (2 nodes pre-warmed for immediate failover).

Key operational plan:
- Canary: route 5% traffic to dedicated pool, ramp to 25% in 48 hours, full cutover after 7 days of stable latency/errors.
- Scale trigger: sustained 5-minute p95 GPU util >75% OR sustained qps >450 for 10 minutes => spin burst up / convert reserves.
- Caching + batching: enable prefix KV caching (expect ~25–35% token savings) and conservative batching to keep tail latency predictable.

Estimated costs (monthly):
- Committed APAC 8 GPUs: ~$52k/mo
- Burstable add (8 GPUs): ~$24k/mo if used ~40% of month
- EU standby 6 GPUs (reserved, low util): ~$36k/mo

I'll follow up with a short SOW draft and a provisioning ETA.

—Jonas
Jonas Weber
Principal Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference

Quick capacity notes from sourcing:

- March shipments have ~65% commit rate due to renewals; earliest provision dates are contingent on signed reserved tranche.
- Recommendation: include a 3-month surge credit clause in the SOW (contractual right to access burst capacity immediately) to mitigate lead-time risk during pilot.

Subject: Re: Pilot capacity ask — infra constraints and model footprint

A few infra items to flag: 
- Model footprint: OrionAI's baseline evals show 48–52 GB peak KV for conversational flows. We recommend A100-80GB equiv or two-node sharded setup to keep KV local and avoid cross-node fetches.
- Networking: ensure SG region has 25 Gbps inter-node links for sustained burst windows; if not, we need to reduce per-node batch sizes to avoid network bottlenecks.
- Canary healthchecks: add token-level latency tracing and a thin-quality-sample pipeline to detect hallucination regressions during early ramp.

I'll coordinate with infra ops on the network checks and confirm whether cross-region failover (to EU warm nodes) requires additional routing rules. ETA for checks: 48 hours.

—Karthik
